methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $31M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
TerraDepth is a Series C-stage transportation company founded by Judson Kauffman and Josef Wolfel that has raised $31.1M to date. The transportation frontier-tech universe includes 8 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, ZeroAvia, and others) and no public comparables, limiting traditional peer-based valuation approaches.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable lens. Using total capital raised ($31.1M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x yields an implied valuation of $53M. This method assumes normal progression dynamics and that raised capital reasonably reflects investor conviction at earlier stages.

The peer-median approach is not applicable: while 3 same-sector companies exist, none meet narrow same-stage or adjacent-stage filters with sufficient density (threshold: ≥3 datapoints), and broad sector medians would introduce excessive noise. The triangulated analysis therefore relies on a single method, supporting a median valuation of $53M with a range of $45M–$61M. Key uncertainties center on whether stage-progression multiples hold in the fragmented transportation subsector, the timing and terms of Series C deployment, and whether peer multiples within transportation will compress or expand. A multi-method view awaits additional comparable data or refined peer segmentation.
